item.title: Dispelling The Myth Of An Idle Wife: Recognition Of The Gendered-burden Of Unpaid Domestic And Care Work In India
item.description: The idea of equating women’s domestic contributions to being idle and therefore not adding value to society is termed as Unpaid Domestic and Care Work (UDCW). The post Dispelling The Myth Of An Idle Wife: Recognition Of The Gendered-burden Of Unpaid Domestic And Care Work In India appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Child Marriage Is Driving A Silent Health Crisis Among Tribal Women And Girls In Kashmir
item.description: In the lush green mountains of Jammu and Kashmir, young women and girls face a silent health crisis due to child marriages, early pregnancies, and poverty. The post Child Marriage Is Driving A Silent Health Crisis Among Tribal Women And Girls In Kashmir appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: An Unnoticed Scene In ‘Ek Chatur Naar’: The Burkha, Stereotypes, And Muslim Identity
item.description: The casual portrayal of a Burkha as a tool for anonymity fuells real anxieties while also strengthening the stereotypes. The post An Unnoticed Scene In ‘Ek Chatur Naar’: The Burkha, Stereotypes, And Muslim Identity appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Crippled Bodies, Climate Disasters: How Climate Change Affects People With Disabilities
item.description: Responding to climate disasters requires moving beyond symbolic inclusion towards twin commitments: climate adaptation that accounts for disability in everyday life, and disaster governance that treats accessibility and participation as enforceable standards rather than aspirational goals. The post Crippled Bodies, Climate Disasters: How Climate Change Affects People With Disabilities appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: AI As Care Worker? The Gendered Cost Of AI Supported Communication
item.description: AI use is booming across demographics, geographies and purposes. The post AI As Care Worker? The Gendered Cost Of AI Supported Communication appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Haunted Histories Of Faith And Dalit Christian Women’s Voices In Malayalam Literature
item.description: From the spectral testimony of Rosykutty to the everyday defiance of schoolgirls, these texts challenge the histories produced by upper-caste Kerala literature, which frequently marginalises or silences Dalit experiences. The post Haunted Histories Of Faith And Dalit Christian Women’s Voices In Malayalam Literature appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Why We Fell In Love With Heated Rivalry’s Shane And Ilya
item.description: Heated Rivalry explores how queer men are forced to navigate the patriarchy and gendered norms and make choices that no one should have to make, such as deciding between a successful career and being with their partner in public. The post Why We Fell In Love With Heated Rivalry’s Shane And Ilya appeared first on Feminism in India.
